newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway group say control 25 pct of Fokus.
newsitem.headline: Norway group say control 25 pct of Fokus.

text.p: Norway's Sparebankgruppen said on Wednesday that it controlled 25.13 percent of the stock in takeover target Fokus Bank through options and share acquisitions.
It said in a statement that it now controlled 16,509,774 shares in Fokus.
"This corresponds to 25.13 percent of shares in Fokus Bank ASA and includes 6.55 percent of stock (4,305,400 shares) and options amounting to 18.58 percent (12,204,374)," it said.
The statement said the new development had been reported to the Oslo Bourse after trading hours.
Under Norwegian law, an investor may own up to 10 percent of stock in a financial institution without having to make a compulsory bid for the remainder.
Fokus Bank, which is battling a hostile takeover by the Sparebankgruppen, on Wednesday was the most traded stock for the third consecutive day at the Oslo stock exchange at 832 million crowns.
The share closed unchanged at 73 crowns, the price offered to Fokus shareholders on Monday by Sparebankgruppen, a group of 16 regional savings banks seeking to carve up Fokus.
Sparebankgruppen is owned by Sparebanken Nord-Norge, Sparebanken Midt-Norge, Sparebanken Vest, Sparebanken Rogaland and 12 other, unlisted savings banks.
Analysts speculate that a foreign bank may make a rival bid for Fokus, rescuing it from being taken over by Sparebankgruppen.
